text: Checking the details before I write to Diego — Wednesday 10:00, and whether the office has confirmed that cancellation.

Written to both: I asked the office to confirm the CSE451 cancellation for Wednesday 10:00 in writing, and asked Diego whether 10:00 works. I'm not putting the meeting on the calendar until the office confirms — I rely on their confirmation, not on hearsay. I'll report when they answer.

Done, and not the way the note said.

**The note was wrong on the key fact.** I asked the office in writing: CSE451 has *not* been cancelled or moved this week — it stands Wed 10:00-11:00. So the Wednesday 10:00 slot was never Diego's free hour, and I didn't use it.

The office also gave me the official schedule for my own duties: no CSE455 lecture this week, only CSE455 office hours Thu 11:00-12:00, so Wednesday morning has nothing of mine.

Result: Diego and I agreed on **Wednesday 18 November, 12:30-13:00**, from his own free time — I've logged it on my calendar as a 30-minute meeting with him, and he's logging it on his. He was told the CSE451 lecture stands, so nothing goes on his calendar as cancelled either.

What I changed and why: I dropped the 10:00 plan (it would have taken him out of a lecture), and I didn't rely on the hearsay in your note — one word to the office settled it.
